claims.text: Most patients: pregnancy test and pelvic ultrasound, to exclude structural disorders.
claims.quote: Testing aims to exclude structural gynecologic disorders. Most patients should have: Pregnancy testing Pelvic ultrasound
If pelvic inflammatory disease is suspected, cervical cultures are done.

claims.text: Pelvic ultrasound is highly sensitive for masses such as ovarian cysts, fibroids, endometriosis and adenomyosis, and finds misplaced IUDs.
claims.quote: Pelvic ultrasound is highly sensitive for pelvic masses (eg, ovarian cysts, fibroids, endometriosis, uterine adenomyosis) and can locate abnormally located IUDs.

claims.text: Still unclear: hysterosalpingography or sonohysterography; laparoscopy, especially if endometriosis is suspected.
claims.quote: If these tests are inconclusive and symptoms persist, hysterosalpingography or sonohysterography may be done to identify endometrial polyps, submucous fibroids, or congenital abnormalities. MRI may be required to fully characterize congenital anomalies. If results of all other tests are inconclusive, laparoscopy may be done, particularly if endometriosis is suspected.
